sentence: S1 (Samuel Adeyemi) is a care coordinator from the community mental health team.
S2 (Hannah Rees) is the person being assessed.
S3 (Tom Whitfield) is Hannah's partner.
The assessment is a care review conducted about six weeks after the last contact.
The last contact was before Bonfire Night, approximately in September.
Hannah has a dog named Pip, a cocker spaniel.
Tom is currently on a work call and will come down after the assessment.
Hannah is currently on sertraline 150mg daily, started on the 10th of November.
Hannah is also taking mirtazapine 15mg at night.
Hannah reports experiencing panic attacks two to three times per week, with some days having a constant hum.
Hannah reports a low mood score of 3 out of 10, with a high of 4 on a good day.
Hannah reported a mood score of 7 during the summer, indicating improvement.
Hannah reports waking up at 3:30 a.m. every night despite taking mirtazapine.
Hannah reports getting only about four hours of sleep per night.
Hannah reports increased hunger, which she attributes to improved eating habits after stopping poor diet.
Hannah lost about half a stone (approximately 22.5 lbs) due to poor eating habits before medication.
Hannah reports a dry mouth as a side effect of mirtazapine.
Hannah takes her medication every day and has not missed any doses.
Tom currently manages the medication boxes and stores them in his drawer upstairs.
Hannah believes the medication is too early to assess for effectiveness, and she wants to continue for six weeks.
Hannah's work is signed off until the 11th of December.
Hannah's manager changed in August, and there was a merger of payroll and accounts, doubling her workload.
Hannah's manager sends emails at 11 p.m. and expects responses by 9 a.m.
Hannah believes her manager has said she is not resilient enough and that her position may be reviewed.
Hannah has an occupational health appointment scheduled for the 2nd of December (phone appointment).
Hannah would consider a phased return to work (e.g., mornings only) if offered, but no such option has been proposed.
Hannah gets up around 7 a.m. when Tom wakes her.
Hannah walks Pip every day as a routine.
Hannah spends most of her day on the sofa and sometimes does not get dressed.
Hannah has not seen any friends recently and has been avoiding social contact.
Hannah Rees denied needing hospital care and stated she is not in the same condition as previously.
The safety plan will include the warning signs: not getting out of bed, stopping walking Pip, going quiet, and not answering Megan.
The crisis line number is currently on the fridge.
Tom Whitfield confirmed the crisis line number is also on his phone.
The care coordinator (Samuel Adeyemi) will refer Hannah to psychology and complete the referral by Friday.
The care coordinator will contact Dr Mensah's secretary to follow up on Hannah's next clinic appointment, as she has not yet had one.
Hannah Rees will complete a sleep diary for the care coordinator, including bedtime, waking time, and duration of nighttime awakenings.
Hannah Rees stated that her friend Jo, who is under the same care team, said the wait for psychology is two years.
The care coordinator stated that the wait for psychology varies and cannot provide a specific number today.
The care coordinator will update the safety plan with a new warning sign (not answering Megan) and will include the week when Tom is away.
The care coordinator advised against assuming the two-year wait for psychology and recommended checking with the service first.
The care coordinator will perform a PHQ-9 mood questionnaire with Hannah, but it will be postponed due to her appearance of being 'shattered'.
Hannah Rees described feeling tired and said Tom 'means well but just panics'.
Hannah Rees expressed frustration about the two-year wait for psychology, saying 'I can't wait two years'.
Tom Whitfield expressed concern that Hannah should be in hospital or have crisis workers come every day, referencing the previous crisis.
Tom Whitfield stated he is scared about Hannah's condition and is unable to monitor her due to being at work.
Hannah Rees agreed to call the crisis line or duty worker if her thoughts become stronger before the follow-up appointment on the eighth of December.
Tom Whitfield will be away from home Monday to Thursday next week due to work in Leeds.
Hannah Rees indicated that Megan may be able to let her stay at her house while Tom is away, but has not decided.
Tom Whitfield expressed interest in a carer's assessment for himself, but said he is not sure and will think about it.
The care coordinator will return for a follow-up appointment on Tuesday, the eighth of December, at 10 o'clock.
The care coordinator will drop a copy of the updated safety plan during the week when Tom is away.
The care coordinator will refer Hannah to psychology and complete the referral by Friday.
